messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx rate detected for customer-newhaven on dedicated-cluster us-west2-prd. 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% to 18% over the last 2m. Alert level: P1.
Maya R: acknowledged, I'm oncall. grabbing dashboards now.
Priya K: pinging runtime logs + routing table, looks like high queue depth on pool gw-usw2-3.
Jorge L: copying logs, seeing KV eviction spikes + repeated `503 gateway` from model-proxy on node g-12. Could be noisy neighbor or GPU OOMs.
Maya R: customer impact? Alex, can you confirm if Newhaven is reporting anything?
Alex T: support said they see timeouts from their app and some 5xx. Their dashboard shows ~15% failed requests since 15:02 UTC. Customer-facing msg in progress.
Maya R: ok plan: 1) quickly route newhaven to fallback pool (lower-cost but compatible model) 2) throttle concurrency to their route 3) open autoscaler request for 2 extra pods 4) keep tracing + logs. Who can do the reroute?
Priya K: I can update routing policy. will flip traffic to pool gw-usw2-burst-1 in 2-3 min. adding a soft limit on concurrency = 6.
Jorge L: i'll take autoscaler and node health. running `ssh runner@g-12` to check process.
Priya K: note: fallback pool uses a quantized variant but preserves API. Informing support.
Maya R: add me to any customer comms.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-537500. Pager duty triggered to SRE Pager.
SRE Pager: on it, stand by for handoff when primary triage done.
Jorge L: on g-12 logs: repeated kernel OOM-killer events around 15:03:21, nvml reports GPU mem spike then driver error, processes restarting, then proxy 502/503. Suspect a single tenant blasting large-batch generation.
Maya R: noisy neighbor hypothesis likely. Priya, can you identify which tenant id maps to those sessions?
Priya K: yes, mapping shows tenant_id=nh-420-heavy on that node, matches Newhaven. Looks like they started a large offline job accidentally hitting prod routing.
Alex T: customer confirms they kicked off a batch fine-tune job by mistake against prod endpoint. They're pausing now.
Maya R: good catch. Immediate mitigations executed: 
- Priya rerouted live traffic for allNewhaven endpoints to gw-usw2-burst-1 (applied at 15:06 UTC)
- Priya applied concurrency limit to newhaven route: 6
- Jorge removed offending process and restarted model-proxy on g-12, cordoned node for investigation
- Autoscaler requested +2 pods, ETA ~6m
Priya K: reroute done. watch metrics for error rate drop.
Jorge L: cordon/drain started on g-12: `kubectl cordon g-12 && kubectl drain g-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Priya K: error rate falling to ~3% after reroute, p50 latency slightly up but acceptable.
Maya R: excellent. Alex please update Newhaven status: request they verify no more batch jobs, advise to use dedicated dedicated-batch queue or schedule during maintenance window.
Alex T: message posted to customer slack + ticket updated.
SRE Pager: handoff: I'll take monitoring for the next 30m and escalate if >5% 5xx persists. Maya, handing off to Priya for post-incident followup.
Priya K: will keep running diagnostics on KV pressure and kernel logs. Suspect KV cache thrash due to large sequence lengths causing backend paging. Opening follow-up ticket to add protective guardrails for large-batch requests.
Maya R: notes for postmortem: root cause = customer-triggered large-batch generation on production routing + lack of route-level batch guardrail. Contributing factors: single node pinned, no soft isolation for heavy tenants on dedicated pools. Mitigation worked: reroute, concurrency throttle, node cordon, scale-out.
Jorge L: saving logs and diagnostic bundle: `tar czf /tmp/nh-incident-537500.tgz /var/log/model-proxy /var/log/kern* /var/log/nvml*` then uploading to S3.
incident-bot: Note: autoscaler added 2 pods at 15:12 UTC.
Priya K: post-mitigation metrics: total request success back to 99.1% for newhaven route, cluster-wide 5xx back to baseline ~0.3%. keeping heightened monitoring 30m.
Alex T: customer confirmed degraded calls dropped to near-zero after pause. Appreciative of rapid response.
Maya R: closing active pager. leaving this thread for postmortem items and remediation tasks. tagging @product to consider model-level quotas and @eng-runtime for stronger tenant isolation. :thumbsup:
Priya K: follow-up action items (quick):
- add route-level max_concurrency default for Dedicated (PR incoming)
- detect large-batch patterns and surface automated soft-quarantine
- improve autoscaler responsiveness for saturated GPUs
Jorge L: I'll add node-level GPU memory monitoring to alert earlier.
SRE Pager: monitoring window complete, no regression. moving to post-incident review.
Maya R: thanks team, good work.
Alex T: will send customer post-incident summary and RFC for suggested workflow if they'd like dedicated batch capacity. :white_check_mark:
